tagline: One-lane bridges carry the road through the rainforest.
intro: From Pāʻia, the Hāna Highway runs east through Haʻikū as Route 36, then carries on as Route 360, a narrow, winding mountain road mostly through tropical rainforest. Route 360 alone has about 620 curves. It passes Keʻanae and Nāhiku on the way to Hāna.

In the sixteenth century the Alaloa, the long road, reached the Hāna District, and its travelers reportedly swung across the streams on vine ropes. The modern road began in the 1870s as an unpaved track for building an irrigation ditch, opened through to Hāna in 1926, and was not completely paved until the 1960s.

moments.title: Pāʻia
moments.text: Surf shops and galleries share a town that once kept a sugar mill working for more than a century.

moments.title: Keʻanae
moments.text: Taro grows on a peninsula made from Haleakalā lava, and a stone church nearby, built in 1856, was one of the few buildings left after the 1946 tsunami.

moments.title: Hāna
moments.text: After the last sugar plantation closed, a new inn helped shift the town toward tourism, with a baseball team brought over for spring training.

practical: Route 360 is narrow and winding, with numerous one-lane road sections and bridges.
